$comment: agent-beeps music craft rules (appliesTo: song). Same shape and meaning as rules.json; beeps song lint checks the auto rules and lists every judgement rule. GUIDE.md section 10 is the reasoning.

rules.statement: The delivered song's true peak is at or below -1 dBTP.

sources.title: EBU R 128: Loudness normalisation and permitted maximum level of audio signals
Audiokinetic: Mastering a Game with Wwise, Part 1 (PlayStation Studios staff)

rules.statement: The delivered song has no clipped samples.

sources.title: Recommendation ITU-R BS.1770-5: Algorithms to measure audio programme loudness and true-peak audio level

rules.statement: The delivered song sits within 2 LU of project.musicLoudness (integrated). A song more than 2 LU under is peak-limited: its transients cap the level.
rules.rationale: No games loudness standard exists; reported platform practice is -24 to -23 LUFS integrated for console and measured shipped games average about -18.5. The -20 LUFS default is this plugin's choice: under the -18 LUFS max-momentary one-shots so sound effects read over music.

sources.title: Schappler: Listening for Loudness in Video Games
Audiokinetic: Mastering a Game with Wwise, Part 1 (PlayStation Studios staff)

rules.statement: Loudness range (EBU Tech 3342) is at most 20 LU, and at least 3 LU for songs longer than a minute.
rules.rationale: 20 LU is the maximum PlayStation staff report for a game mix. The 3 LU floor is this plugin's: a minute of music with no dynamic contour does not breathe, and it is the first thing listeners tire of.

sources.title: Audiokinetic: Mastering a Game with Wwise, Part 1 (PlayStation Studios staff)

rules.statement: A loop song's level steps no more than 3 dB across the loop point (last 400 ms against first 400 ms).
rules.rationale: The 3 dB bound is this plugin's. The render folds the tail onto the start, so the seam is continuous in time; a level jump is what remains audible as a restart.

sources.title: Collins, Game Sound (MIT Press, 2008), ch. 2 and 8: looping and variability

rules.statement: A loop song lasts at least 60 s when tagged exploration, ambient or level, and at least 20 s otherwise.
rules.rationale: Collins finds loop length set by how long the player stays: the longest-played genres had the longest loops, boss music the shortest. The second counts are this plugin's.

sources.title: Collins, Game Sound (MIT Press, 2008), ch. 2 p. 27

rules.statement: Energy below 120 Hz is at most 40% of the song's spectrum, and at least 2%.
rules.rationale: Both bounds are this plugin's. Composer testing found songs at 47% low share whose spectrograms showed a solid 50-110 Hz band and a 175 Hz centroid: muddy. Low end masks everything above it and eats headroom; a song with none sounds thin on good speakers.

sources.title: Robjohns (Sound on Sound): Can static EQ tackle masking effectively?

rules.statement: Pitched notes stay between E1 (41 Hz) and C8 (4186 Hz).
rules.rationale: Both bounds are this plugin's. Below E1 a note is felt more than heard, reads as rumble on good speakers and vanishes on laptops and phones; above C8 it is a whistle. Notes outside the range are almost always an octave slip.

sources.title: Robjohns (Sound on Sound): Can static EQ tackle masking effectively?

rules.statement: Every track and pattern is played somewhere in the form.
rules.rationale: Dead parts are usually a typo in a section's play map, not a choice.

sources.title: Robjohns (Sound on Sound): Can static EQ tackle masking effectively?

rules.statement: Parts that play together sit in different registers or leave each other rhythmic gaps; fix a masking clash in the arrangement (voicing, octave, rhythm) before the mix.

sources.title: Robjohns (Sound on Sound): Can static EQ tackle masking effectively?

rules.statement: Music heard for a long time (exploration, menus) keeps melody understated, varies its sections, and leaves space: rests, thinned sections, slow fades in rather than an abrupt start.

sources.title: Collins, Game Sound (MIT Press, 2008), ch. 8: listener fatigue and variability
